cards.title: Entity lineage and foreign key propagation across maintenance tables
cards.body:
The maintenance workflow links equipment master, work permit, order, and issue tables across database schemas.
fPermitMaster records establish PermitId keys consumed by fEquipmentMaster and fMaintenanceOrder entities.
fMaintenanceOrder headers store EquipmentId and reference source MaintenanceRequestId rows through foreign keys.
Detail tables EAM.EAMOrderItemDetail store ItemId and RequiredQty for spare component planning and reservation.
Material issues in Inventory.IMaterialIssue reference MaintenanceOrderId to close demand lines upon parts disbursement.
Work order task rows in EAM.EAMOrderTaskDetail maintain foreign keys referencing masterdata.mTaskMaster.
Audit fields capture OrderDate, CompletionDate, and DownTimeHours to calculate reliability metrics.
This relational key propagation ensures complete lineage reporting from permit configuration to spares consumption.

cards.title: Status cascading and material demand closure across PM and inventory
cards.body:
Maintenance order authorization triggers status updates across upstream requests and linked inventory tables.
fMaintenanceRequest rows transition DocumentStatus from Open to In-Progress or Ordered in the database.
Authorizing the linked material issue decrements open spare requirements on the maintenance order detail rows.
When all required tasks and material lines are satisfied, the order transitions to Completed status automatically.
Completing the order updates downtime logs and recalculates equipment availability metrics within EAM reporting tables.
Cancelling a maintenance order invokes balance restoration routines that release reserved stores inventory.
Status recalculations execute within atomic database transactions to ensure consistency between orders and stock.
This synchronization prevents orphan material requisitions and unfulfilled maintenance job allocations.

cards.title: Backend stored procedure architecture and transaction coordination
cards.body:
Maintenance operations execute through specialized stored procedures operating within the EAM schema.
Work order persistence invokes EAM.EAMOSave which orchestrates header and detail insertions in the database.
Task line operations execute through EAM.EAMOrderTaskDetailSave within the same transaction scope.
Parts requisition routines interface with Inventory.IIndentRequisitionSave to stage stores demand lines.
Database rollback triggers ensure order headers and requisition links commit synchronously without partial writes.
Lookup routines like EAM.EAMOFillValues populate user dropdowns and equipment filters efficiently.
Delete handlers invoke EAM.EAMODelete which validates downstream reporting and issue references prior to row removal.
This modular stored procedure architecture ensures robust transaction processing and audit tracking.

cards.title: Multi-level authorization workflows and document state locking in PM
cards.body:
Maintenance orders transition through Initial, Release, and Authorized lifecycle states during processing.
Authorization groups enforce user tier limits configured in masterdata.mAuthorizationGroup and user mapping tables.
Intermediate sign-offs record audit entries in EAM.EAMOrderApprovalHistory without full authorization.
Only designated chief maintenance engineers can transition document status to Authorized in the database.
Authorized status triggers database triggers that make task lists and equipment references immutable.
Amendments require formal revision entries in EAM.EAMOrderAmendment rather than direct updates to authorized orders.
Audit triggers record prior row states to historical archive tables before status transitions execute.
This security architecture protects maintenance schedules and safety check lists from unauthorized alteration.
